findings.title: Sales-invoice PDF names the CA FIRM as the supplier, with the CA firm's GSTIN and PAN, on the client's own sale
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/invoice_pdf_service.py:355 `firm = _load_firm(firm_id)` reads `public.firms` (the CA practice / tenant) and passes it to `build_invoice_pdf(invoice_dict, firm, customer)`; lines 148-160 render that row as the supplier block — `firm.get("name")`, `GSTIN: {firm['gstin']}`, `PAN: {firm['pan']}` — under the heading "TAX INVOICE ... Section 31, CGST Act 2017". The builder was written for `fee_invoices` (the practice billing its own clients — services/invoice_generation_service.py, repositories/invoice_repository.py) and `get_sales_invoice_pdf` reuses it verbatim for `client_sales_invoices`, whose supplier is the CLIENT. That the client is the supplier is settled by routers/sales_invoices.py:680 `client_state_code = _get_state_code_from_gstin(client_rec.get("gstin"))` — intra/inter-state is decided by the CLIENT's GSTIN. tests/test_invoice_pdf_line_items.py:193 pins the wrong behaviour (`_load_firm` stubbed to `{"name": "Test & Co", "gstin": "27AAAAA9999A1Z5"}`). The same PDF is emailed to the customer (routers/sales_invoices.py:1965) and served on the client portal (routers/portal_data.py:54). services/statement_pdf_service.py:104-105 has the identical defect on the customer statement. apps/api/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:22-36 shows `clients` already carries client_name, pan, gstin, address, state, state_code.
findings.ca_experience: The CA emails their client's customer a tax invoice headed with the CA practice's name and the practice's GSTIN. The customer's accountant tries to claim ITC against a GSTIN that never made the supply, and it will not match GSTR-2B. If any such PDF is used as the tax invoice of record it is a Rule 46(a)/(b) failure for the client and a misuse of the practice's own registration.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all print the COMPANY whose books are open as the supplier. In Zoho Books Practice the accountant's own branding never appears on the client's outward invoice.
findings.suggested_fix: In `get_sales_invoice_pdf`, load `public.clients` by `invoice.client_id` (firm-scoped) and pass THAT as the supplier; keep `_load_firm` only for the `fee_invoices` path in `get_invoice_pdf`. Rename `build_invoice_pdf(invoice, supplier, recipient)` so the two callers cannot be confused again, and change the test stub so it fails on the old behaviour. Same change in `statement_pdf_service.get_customer_statement_pdf`.

verification.probe: read invoice_pdf_service.py:355 _load_firm(firm_id) rendered as the supplier block at :148-160

findings.title: Invoice PDF prints a hardcoded 18% / 9% / 9% tax rate on every invoice regardless of the actual line rates
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/invoice_pdf_service.py:30 `GST_RATE_PCT = 18`; lines 223-226 emit `f"CGST @ {GST_RATE_PCT // 2}%"`, `f"SGST @ {GST_RATE_PCT // 2}%"`, `f"IGST @ {GST_RATE_PCT}%"`. The AMOUNTS come from the stored heads (correct), but the printed RATE is the constant. The line table (rows built at 199-214) carries only `#`, `Description`, `SAC`, `Taxable Value` — no quantity, no unit, no per-line rate, no per-line tax. The frontend by contrast gets this right: components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:604-612 only shows `@ x%` when `uniformRate != null`, i.e. when every line shares one rate.
findings.ca_experience: A 5% invoice (or a 12% one, or a mixed-rate one) prints "CGST @ 9% ... SGST @ 9%" beside a 5% amount. The customer's team sees a document whose stated rate and stated tax do not reconcile; a GST officer reading it sees a Rule 46(l) defect. On a goods invoice the missing quantity and unit are further Rule 46(g)/(h) defects.
findings.market_standard: Every tool in the market (Tally Prime, Zoho Books, Busy, Marg) prints a rate-wise tax summary derived from the lines, plus quantity, UQC and per-line rate/tax columns, because Rule 46 requires them.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete `GST_RATE_PCT`. Group the invoice's lines by `gst_rate_bps` and emit one CGST/SGST or IGST row per rate band, labelled from the band. Add Qty, Unit, Rate and per-line tax columns to the line table. Add a regression test that renders a 5% invoice and asserts "9%" does not appear.

findings.title: Invoice PDF always states "tax payable on reverse charge basis: No", and never prints the place of supply or the IRN/QR
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/invoice_pdf_service.py:253-254 `story.append(Paragraph("Whether tax is payable on reverse charge basis: No", ...))` — an unconditional string. `is_reverse_charge` is a real, CA-settable column (migration 268; models/invoices.py:139; components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:766-770) and is plumbed correctly into GSTR-1 (`domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:232 "rchrg": "Y" if inv.is_reverse_charge else "N"`), so the PDF is the only place that contradicts it. `get_sales_invoice_pdf`'s `invoice_dict` (lines 331-345) never carries `supply_state_code`, and `build_invoice_pdf` never prints a place of supply. No IRN/QR is rendered anywhere in the module even though `einvoice_records.irn`/`qr_data` exist (domain/income_tax/einvoice_service.py:154-160).
findings.ca_experience: An RCM invoice — the exact document where the declaration matters — carries a printed statement saying the opposite. Rule 46(p). The recipient reading "No" may not self-assess. An inter-state invoice carries no place of supply (Rule 46(n)). Once e-invoicing applies to the client, Rule 48(5) makes an invoice without the IRN QR not an invoice at all, and this PDF can never carry one.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books print the reverse-charge declaration from the voucher's own flag, print Place of Supply on every invoice, and stamp the IRN + signed QR onto the PDF once the IRN is returned.
findings.suggested_fix: Read `is_reverse_charge` into `invoice_dict` and render Yes/No from it; add a Place of Supply line (state code + name); when a `generated` einvoice_record exists for the invoice, render the IRN, Ack No/date and the QR from `qr_data`.

findings.title: Deleting a middle draft credit note (or sales debit note) permanently wedges that client's numbering for the rest of the financial year
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/credit_notes.py:111-119 `_next_cn_seq` returns `count(credit_notes LIKE 'CN-{fy}-%') + 1` — a COUNT, not a max. routers/credit_notes.py:652-737 `delete_credit_note` hard-deletes a draft (`db.table("credit_notes").delete()`), and the number was already assigned at create (line 322 `insert_numbered_document_with_lines`). migrations/151_per_client_document_numbering.sql:93-94 puts UNIQUE (firm_id, client_id, credit_note_no) on the table. services/numbering.py:80-97 retries 6 times but re-calls the SAME `next_seq`, which returns the same value every time. Reproduced against the repo's own test double (tests/test_document_numbering_unit._FakeDB): with CN-2627-0001/0002/0003 present, deleting 0002 makes `_next_cn_seq` return 3 forever — `retry sequence values: [3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3]`, colliding with the live CN-2627-0003 on every attempt. routers/sales_debit_notes.py:121-128 `_next_sdn_seq` and services/receipt_service.py:70-80 `_next_receipt_seq` are the identical shape.
findings.ca_experience: The CA raises three credit notes, deletes the middle draft as a mistake, and from then on every attempt to create a credit note for that client fails with a generic "Unable to complete credit note operation" until the financial year rolls over. There is no message telling them why and no way out from the UI.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books derive the next voucher number from the highest number in the series (or a dedicated sequence), so a deleted voucher leaves a gap and never blocks the next one.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the sequence from the MAX numeric suffix in the series for (firm, client, FY) rather than a row count — or move to a Postgres sequence per (firm, client, series, FY) as `next_invoice_number` (migration 124) already does for fee invoices. Add a test that creates three notes, deletes the second, and asserts the fourth is created successfully.

findings.title: The Sales screen's "Outstanding" tile overstates receivables — it sums the full invoice total for partially-paid invoices and ignores credit notes entirely
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:1439-1443: `let outstanding = 0 ... if (inv.status === "issued" || inv.status === "partially_paid") outstanding += inv.total_paise;` — `paid_paise` is fetched (line 1372 select list, mapped at 1424) and simply not subtracted, and `credited_paise` / `debit_note_paise` are not even selected. The backend already computes this correctly: routers/sales_invoices.py:344-348 `outstanding = sum(total + debit_note - paid - credited)`, and migration 278 added an `outstanding_paise` generated column for exactly this. Rendered at page.tsx:1856 `<SummaryCard label="Outstanding" value={fmt(stats.outstanding)} />`.
findings.ca_experience: A client with ₹10,00,000 invoiced, ₹8,00,000 collected on account and ₹50,000 credited sees "Outstanding ₹10,00,000" on the Sales dashboard instead of ₹1,50,000. Every partial payment and every credit note makes the number worse. The CA reads the tile, reports the receivable to the client, and it is wrong.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books' Invoices dashboard shows Total Outstanding as balance due (invoice total less payments and credits applied); Tally's Bills Outstanding report is pending-amount based.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `GET /api/sales-invoices/outstanding?client_id=…` for the tile (the endpoint exists and is correct), or select `outstanding_paise` (migration 278) and sum it. Do not recompute the formula in TypeScript — that is what let it drift.

findings.title: Goa, Puducherry, Ladakh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar cannot be selected as place of supply or as a customer's state
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/invoices/gst.ts:217-233 defines a SECOND `INDIAN_STATES` list containing only 01-24, 27, 29, 32, 33, 36, 37 — Goa (30), DNH&DD (26), Puducherry (34), Ladakh (38), Lakshadweep (31) and A&N (35) are absent, as are 96/97. components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:41 imports `INDIAN_STATES` from `@/lib/invoices/shared` (which re-exports `./gst` at lib/invoices/shared.ts:12) and passes it explicitly at line 715 `<StateLookup states={INDIAN_STATES} …>`, overriding the CORRECT canonical list that StateLookup defaults to (components/lookups/StateLookup.tsx:4 → lib/constants/indianStates.ts:10-45, which has Goa, DNH&DD, Puducherry and Ladakh). components/customers/CustomerFormModal.tsx:23,197 does the same for the customer's State Code. The backend accepts all of 01-38 plus 96/97 (apps/api/domain/gst/validator.py:18-25).
findings.ca_experience: A Goa customer cannot be given a state code. `state_code` stays blank, so on invoice creation `effective_supply_state = supply_state_code or customer.state_code or ""` (routers/sales_invoices.py:672) is empty, `is_interstate` evaluates False (line 677), and a Maharashtra client billing a Goa customer is charged CGST+SGST instead of IGST — a wrong tax on a real invoice. The error only surfaces much later, when the GSTR-1 validator rejects the blank place of supply (domain/gst/validator.py:93-99).
findings.market_standard: Every Indian accounting product ships the full 38-entry GST state/UT master plus 96/97 (Other Territory / Other Country) and derives the state from the GSTIN prefix as a fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate list in lib/invoices/gst.ts and re-export `lib/constants/indianStates`; add 31 (Lakshadweep), 35 (Andaman & Nicobar), 97 (Other Territory) and 96 (Other Country) to the canonical list; drop the explicit `states={INDIAN_STATES}` props so StateLookup's default is used. Separately, default `customers.state_code` from `gstin[:2]` server-side when it is blank.

findings.title: TDS deducted by the customer (§194J / §194Q) cannot be recorded on a receipt from any screen
findings.evidence: `ReceiptIn.tds_paise` exists (apps/api/models/invoices.py:394) and the whole settlement engine honours it — services/receipt_service.py:533-535 `settlement = amount_paise + tds_paise`, services/phase2_journal_service.py:206-238 posts Dr Bank + Dr TDS Receivable / Cr Trade Receivables. But the receipt form never sends it: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:3470-3480 posts only `client_id, customer_id, receipt_date, amount_paise, payment_mode, reference_no, allocations, currency, exchange_rate`. `grep -rn "tds_paise" apps/web/app apps/web/lib apps/web/components` returns hits only in payroll, purchases and the TDS module — nothing in the sales receipt path. The screen's own "Unallocated" line (page.tsx:3629) computes `amountPaise - totalAllocated`, which is the wrong basis even if TDS were entered.
findings.ca_experience: On a ₹1,00,000 professional-fee invoice the customer pays ₹90,000 and deducts ₹10,000 TDS — the normal case for almost every B2B service invoice in India. The CA can only record ₹90,000. The invoice stays `partially_paid` with ₹10,000 outstanding forever, AR is overstated by the TDS on every invoice, the TDS Receivable asset is never booked, and there is nothing to reconcile against Form 26AS. The only workaround is a manual journal, outside the sub-ledger.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's receipt voucher takes a TDS deduction line against the bill; Zoho Books has an explicit "TDS deducted" field on Record Payment that closes the invoice and books TDS receivable. This is table stakes for an Indian receivables module.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a TDS Deducted (₹) field to ReceiptForm, parsed with `paiseFromRupeeInput`, sent as `tds_paise`; change the Unallocated display to `amount + tds - allocated` to match `create_receipt_core`; show the settlement value beside the cash amount so the CA can see the invoice will close.

findings.title: Every receipt debits one firm-wide "Bank" ledger — cash receipts land in Bank, and the selected bank account is discarded
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:210 `bank_id = self._find_account(db, firm_id, client_id, "%Bank%", system_key="bank")` — unconditional; `receipt["payment_mode"]` (bank/cash/cheque/upi/neft/rtgs/online) is read at services/receipt_service.py:632 into the row but never consulted when building the journal. `_find_account`'s system_key branch (phase2_journal_service.py:1423-1435) filters on firm_id + system_account_key only, with no client or account filter, so it returns one ledger for the whole firm. `ReceiptIn.bank_account_id` (models/invoices.py:400) is accepted by the API and then dropped — it is absent from the `receipt_payload` dict built at services/receipt_service.py:623-637, so it is never even stored. The frontend never sends it either (app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:3470-3480).
findings.ca_experience: A cash sale receipt is posted to the Bank ledger, so the client's cash book is understated and the bank ledger overstated by every cash collection. A client with two bank accounts has all receipts posted to one of them, so the bank reconciliation for the other account can never tie and the first shows deposits that never hit the statement.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's Receipt voucher requires the cash/bank ledger to be selected and posts to it. Zoho Books requires "Deposit To" on every payment received.
findings.suggested_fix: Store `bank_account_id` on the receipt, resolve the debit ledger from it, and fall back to the Cash-in-Hand ledger when `payment_mode == "cash"`. Make the Deposit To / Cash account a required field on the receipt form.

findings.title: GSTR-1 Table 11A/11B (tax on advances, §13(2)) is unreachable — the three columns it needs are never written by any code path
findings.evidence: migrations/286_advance_receipt_gst.sql:48-53 adds `receipts.gst_rate_bps`, `receipts.place_of_supply`, `receipts.is_interstate` and `clients.gst_advance_tax_applicable`. services/gst_advance_service.py:143-155 reads them and does `if rate is None or not pos: continue` for every receipt. But `ReceiptIn` (models/invoices.py:380-410) has no such fields, `create_receipt_core`'s `receipt_payload` (services/receipt_service.py:623-637) and `create_foreign_receipt`'s (line 236) omit them, and `grep -rn "gst_rate_bps" apps/api/services apps/api/routers` finds no writer for the receipts table. The frontend never sends them either. The only place they are ever set is the test fixture itself — tests/test_gstr1_advances_are_surfaced.py:163 seeds them straight into the DB, so the feature is green in CI and dead in production.
findings.ca_experience: A client who supplies services and takes advances turns on "tax liability on advance receipts", and GSTR-1 Table 11A still comes out empty. The advance is visible only in the informational advances report (which itself reports `table_11_computed: false`, gst_advance_service.py:230), so tax on advances under §13(2) is simply never declared — an under-declaration on a filed return.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's "Enable tax liability on advance receipts" prompts for the rate and place of supply on the receipt voucher and fills Table 11A/11B; ClearTax GST picks it up from the advance ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `gst_rate_bps`, `place_of_supply`, `is_interstate` to `ReceiptIn` and to the receipt payload, defaulting place of supply from the customer's state; show the three fields on the receipt form only when the client's `gst_advance_tax_applicable` is true (the migration's own stated design). Then make `advances_report` report `table_11_computed: true` for those clients.

findings.title: Export/SEZ invoices produce a GSTR-1 the portal will reject — shipping bill number, date and port code are hardcoded empty, and SEZ/deemed exports are filed as ordinary exports
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:538-549 builds Table 6A with `"sbpcode": ""`, `"sbnum": ""`, `"sbdt": ""` — literals, because `client_sales_invoices` has no column for them (no shipping-bill columns anywhere in migrations/, and none in models/invoices.py `SalesInvoiceIn`). domain/gst/classifier.py:110-124 maps `SEZ_with_payment`/`SEZ_without_payment`/`Deemed_export` onto `EXP_WP`/`EXP_WOP`, and gstr1_builder's table map (lines 6-14) has only `6A → EXP` — there is no Table 6B (SEZ) or 6C (Deemed export) builder at all. The classifier's own comment even says `Deemed_export` "defaults to WOPAY (conservative)".
findings.ca_experience: An exporter client's GSTR-1 is offered with blank shipping-bill details, so the return cannot be matched to ICEGATE for the IGST refund under §16(3) and the portal flags the rows. An SEZ supply — with or without payment — is filed in Table 6A as an ordinary export, so the SEZ unit's own refund/ITC claim has nothing to match against, and a deemed export is filed as an export, which it is not.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime captures shipping bill no/date/port code on the export invoice and fills 6A; ClearTax and Zoho Books both separate 6A (Exports), 6B (SEZ) and 6C (Deemed exports).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `shipping_bill_no`, `shipping_bill_date`, `port_code` columns and editor fields (shown when supply_type is zero_rated), feed them into `_build_exp`, and add `_build_sez` / `_build_deemed_export` with their own GSTInvoiceCategory values so 6B and 6C are emitted instead of being folded into 6A.

findings.title: No discount field anywhere on a sales invoice — not per line, not at document level
findings.evidence: `InvoiceLineIn` (apps/api/models/invoices.py:33-58) has description, hsn_sac, quantity, unit, rate_paise, gst_rate_percent, is_service, service_catalogue_id — and no discount. `client_sales_invoice_lines` (migrations/050_sales_purchase_cycle.sql:58-74) has no discount column, and no later migration adds one (`grep -rn "discount" apps/api/routers apps/api/models apps/api/services apps/api/domain/gst` returns nothing but an unrelated comment in models/inventory.py:12). The editor's line table (components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:843-851) has Product/Service, Description, HSN/SAC, Qty, Unit, Rate, GST %, Amount — no discount column.
findings.ca_experience: A trading client who gives a 5% line discount, or a 2% cash discount on the footer, cannot record the invoice as it was actually raised. The CA has to net the discount into the rate, which loses the disclosure the customer's own copy shows and makes the invoice un-reconcilable to the client's price list. CGST §15(3)(a) allows a pre-supply discount shown on the invoice to be excluded from the value of supply — with no field, the arithmetic has to be done by hand off-system.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime has a Discount column (percentage or amount) on every invoice line plus ledger-level discounts; Zoho Books has line discounts, document-level discount and "discount before/after tax"; Busy and Marg both have scheme/trade/cash discount slabs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `discount_percent_bps` and `discount_paise` to the line (with an invoice-level discount that allocates pro-rata to lines), make `taxable_amount_paise = qty × rate − discount` in `_create_invoice_core` and in `lib/money/gstLine.ts`, regenerate `shared/gst-parity-vectors.json`, and print the discount column on the PDF.

findings.title: Sales invoice numbering is entirely manual; the Invoice Settings numbering series a CA configures in the UI is read by nothing on this path
findings.evidence: apps/api/models/invoices.py:11-16 and routers/sales_invoices.py:127-134 state the decision: "numbering is fully manual (the CA types it — no Caflow-generated scheme)". Meanwhile routers/branding.py:43-56 exposes `PUT /api/settings/invoice-settings` with `prefix`, `include_financial_year`, `sequence_length`, `starting_number`, `manual_override_allowed`, surfaced at apps/web/app/settings/page.tsx:663 and wired at apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:2018-2020. The only reader is repositories/invoice_repository.py:149-152 — and that serves `fee_invoices` (the practice's own billing), never `client_sales_invoices`. Unattended generation is worse: services/numbering.py:18-28 `draft_placeholder_invoice_no()` returns `DRAFT-<10 hex>` and services/recurring_invoice_service.py:477 stamps that onto every generated recurring invoice.
findings.ca_experience: For every invoice on every client the CA types the number by hand and hopes it is consecutive — Rule 46(b) requires a consecutive serial. Gaps and repeats are the CA's problem to notice; the app only rejects an exact duplicate, after the fact. Recurring invoicing, the one feature that should remove this work, hands back drafts numbered `DRAFT-A1B2C3D4E5` that must each be renumbered by hand before issue. And a CA who configures a numbering series in Settings gets no effect at all, with nothing saying so.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime has automatic voucher numbering with per-FY reset, prefix/suffix and a duplicate/gap warning; Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all auto-number with a configurable series per document type and per branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `client_sales_invoices` a per-(firm, client, series, FY) sequence (the pattern `next_invoice_number`, migration 124, already uses for fee invoices), pre-fill the editor's Invoice Number from it while leaving it editable when `manual_override_allowed`, and use it for recurring generation instead of `DRAFT-…`. Until then, either wire Invoice Settings to this path or remove the Settings page so it does not promise something it cannot do.

findings.title: Firm branding, invoice templates, bank/UPI details and footer text are stored by a full Settings UI that nothing ever reads
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "branding" apps/api/services apps/api/routers apps/api/domain` returns only routers/branding.py itself — no consumer. The router persists logo_url, colours, font (lines 33-41), five template types (line 25 `_VALID_TEMPLATE_TYPES`), logo position/header/footer/signature placement (lines 58-66), and bank_name / account_number / ifsc_code / upi_id / upi_qr_url / footer_text (lines 48-56). `services/invoice_pdf_service.build_invoice_pdf` imports none of it — the PDF is a fixed reportlab layout with a `#1f2937` header and no logo. The screens exist: apps/web/app/settings/page.tsx:663 and :679 link to `/settings/invoice-settings` and `/settings/invoice-templates`, with a full API client at apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:2000-2031. The email templates (`/api/settings/email-templates`) are likewise unread — services/email_service.py is not among the grep hits.
findings.ca_experience: The CA uploads the client's logo, picks the "Professional CA" template, enters the client's bank account, IFSC and UPI QR for the customer to pay against, and writes footer terms — then downloads the invoice and none of it is there. The customer receives an unbranded document with no payment instructions, which is the single most common reason an SME invoice does not get paid on time.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books ships 16 invoice templates with logo, colour and font control plus bank details and a UPI QR block; Tally Prime has configurable print with company logo and bank details; Marg and Busy both have designer templates.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire it up — load `firm_branding` + `invoice_settings` in `get_sales_invoice_pdf`, draw the logo and accent colour, and add a Bank Details / UPI QR / footer block — or take the Settings pages down until it is. Add a test asserting the configured footer text appears in the rendered PDF, so it cannot silently detach again.

findings.title: An unallocated advance receipt can never be applied to a later invoice from any screen, and it never becomes a party credit
findings.evidence: `PUT /api/receipts/{receipt_id}/allocations` exists and is correct — routers/receipts.py:250-330 reverses prior allocations, re-validates each against live outstanding and re-applies. `grep -rn "/allocations" apps/web/app apps/web/lib apps/web/components` returns nothing; the only receipt call besides create is `POST /api/receipts/{id}/reverse` (app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:3204). Separately, party credit is granted ONLY from the bank-matching path — `grep -rn "grant_credit" apps/api` finds one caller, services/bank_posting_service.py:669 — so a manually entered over-payment sits in `receipts.unallocated_paise` and never reaches `party_credit_balances`, which is the balance the Statements tab's "Apply credit" flow reads (app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:1000, 1029).
findings.ca_experience: A customer pays ₹5,00,000 on account in March against invoices not yet raised. The CA records the receipt with no allocation. In April the invoices go out and there is no way to apply that advance to them — the receipt shows Unallocated ₹5,00,000 forever, the new invoices show fully outstanding, and the customer statement double-counts. The only route is to reverse the receipt and re-enter it, which changes the receipt number and the posting date.
findings.market_standard: Tally's bill-wise details let you settle a new bill against an existing On-Account/Advance reference; Zoho Books shows "Use this advance payment" / "Apply credits" directly on the invoice.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an "Allocate" action on a receipt row that opens the open-invoice list and calls `PUT /api/receipts/{id}/allocations`, and surface `unallocated_paise` as an advance on the customer statement beside the party-credit balance (or unify the two by granting a party credit when a receipt is left unallocated).

findings.title: Credit notes, sales debit notes and receipts can be posted into a period whose GSTR-1 has already been filed — only invoices are guarded
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "period_lock_service" apps/api/routers apps/api/services` returns only routers/sales_invoices.py:825 (create), :1252-1254 (update) and routers/purchase_bills.py:1345-1347. routers/credit_notes.py imports `period_validation_service` only (line 19) and calls `validate_posting_date` at :271 (create), :434 (update) and :506 (issue) — the FY lock, never `assert_open`. routers/sales_debit_notes.py:203, :318, :378 likewise. services/receipt_service.py:548 likewise. routers/sales_invoices.py:1478 (`issue_invoice`) also calls only `validate_posting_date`, so a draft created before a return was filed can still be issued into that filed period.
findings.ca_experience: The CA files GSTR-1 for July, then in September posts a July-dated credit note against a July invoice. Nothing objects. July's outward supply figures in the books no longer agree with the July return that was filed, and the correction that should have gone in a later period's amendment tables (CGST §37) has silently rewritten a closed one. The invoice screen refuses the same thing, so the behaviour is inconsistent and the CA has no reason to expect it.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and Zoho Books both lock a GST period once the return is marked filed and force corrections into an amendment. Tally Prime warns on altering a voucher in a period marked as returns-filed.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `period_lock_service.assert_open(db, firm_id, client_id, date)` on credit-note create/update/issue, sales-debit-note create/update/issue, receipt create, and in `issue_invoice` (re-checking at issue, not just at create).

findings.title: Nothing checks that a reverse-charge or nil/exempt invoice actually carries zero tax, so the books and GSTR-1 disagree
findings.evidence: `_create_invoice_core` computes GST purely from `gst_rate_bps` and `is_interstate` (routers/sales_invoices.py:719-724); `supply_type`, `invoice_type` and `is_reverse_charge` are stored (lines 887-892) and never influence the tax. On the return side, `domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:415-430` (`_build_nil_exempt`) reports only `taxable_amount_paise` into nil_amt/expt_amt/ngsup_amt — the CGST/SGST/IGST heads on such an invoice are silently dropped. `domain/gst/validator.py:82-145` checks CGST=SGST, IGST-vs-interstate and tax arithmetic, but never supply_type-vs-tax or reverse-charge-vs-tax. The editor warns that the classification is non-standard (InvoiceEditor.tsx:777-785) but does not check the rates.
findings.ca_experience: The CA ticks "Exempt" (or "Reverse charge") on an invoice and leaves the lines at 18%. The invoice posts CGST/SGST Output to the ledger and the customer is charged tax. GSTR-1 then declares the supply as exempt with no tax at all (or as rchrg=Y, meaning the recipient owes it). The GST payable in the books and the GST declared on the return differ by the whole amount, and nothing anywhere says so until a reconciliation is attempted.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime refuses to save a voucher whose GST classification and tax ledgers conflict and shows it under "Incomplete/Mismatch in information"; ClearTax's GSTR-1 validation flags a nil/exempt row carrying tax.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_create_invoice_core` and the credit/debit-note equivalents, reject (or require an explicit override on) an invoice where `supply_type in (nil_rated, exempt, non_gst)` or `is_reverse_charge` is true and any line's `gst_rate_bps > 0`. Add the same check to `GSTValidator.validate_invoice` so a legacy row is caught before the return is built.

findings.title: The e-way bill threshold is tested against taxable value instead of consignment value including tax, so invoices over ₹50,000 are advised as "not required"
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/invoices/compliance.ts:22 `export const EWAY_THRESHOLD_PAISE = 5_000_000;` and lines 168-170: `if (inv.taxable_amount_paise < EWAY_THRESHOLD_PAISE) warnings.push("Taxable value is below ₹50,000 — an E-Way Bill is usually not required.")`. `compInv.taxable_amount_paise` is fed from `invoice.taxable_amount_paise` (components/invoices/CompliancePanel.tsx:52), i.e. the value BEFORE GST. Rule 138(1) Explanation 2 defines consignment value as the §15 value declared in the invoice INCLUDING central/State/integrated tax and cess. Confirmed by tests/compliance.test.ts:54-55, which asserts the below-threshold behaviour against the taxable value.
findings.ca_experience: A goods invoice with ₹48,000 taxable and ₹8,640 IGST is a ₹56,640 consignment and needs an e-way bill. The Compliance panel tells the CA it is "below ₹50,000 — usually not required". If the CA relies on it, the goods move without an e-way bill; §129 detention and a penalty of the tax plus an equal amount follow.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books both test the invoice total (value including tax) against ₹50,000 and prompt for e-way bill details at that point.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `total_paise` (or taxable + all tax heads, excluding exempt lines) against the threshold, and cite Rule 138(1) Explanation 2 in the message. Move the rule to the backend — see SALES-18.

findings.title: Statutory rules live in TypeScript with no backend counterpart, against the house rule "zero business logic in the frontend"
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/invoices/compliance.ts is a 296-line statutory module: the Rule 138 ₹50,000 threshold (line 22), Rule 48(4) IRN eligibility including the B2B/export/SEZ scope test (lines 141-160), e-way eligibility (163-178), place-of-supply validation with its own valid-state-code range (lines 13-18, 97-118) and a THIRD GSTIN regex (line 20) — distinct both from apps/web/lib/gst/gstin.ts (which is pinned to the backend by apps/api/tests/fixtures/gstin.json) and from apps/api/domain/gst/gstin.py. `grep -rn "irn_eligib|eway_eligib|EWAY_THRESHOLD|Rule 138" apps/api` finds nothing but a docstring in routers/eway_bill.py:2. So these rules exist in exactly one place and it is the browser bundle, with no parity test and no server-side enforcement. SALES-17 is what that costs.
findings.ca_experience: Not visible directly, but it is why SALES-17 exists and stayed: a wrong threshold in a TypeScript file has no Python twin to disagree with it and no parity vector to fail. Every future change to an IRN or e-way rule has to be made by someone who thinks to look in apps/web.
findings.market_standard: Not a market comparison — this is the repo's own stated rule (CLAUDE.md, "Code rules": computation, validation and statutory rules live in apps/api), which the money layer (lib/money/gstLine.ts pinned by shared/gst-parity-vectors.json) already honours properly.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `irnEligibility` / `ewayEligibility` / `validatePlaceOfSupply` into `apps/api/domain/gst/` behind an endpoint the panel calls, or — if a live preview is wanted — keep the mirror but pin it with a generated fixture the way `shared/gst-parity-vectors.json` pins the GST arithmetic. Collapse the third GSTIN regex onto lib/gst/gstin.ts.

findings.title: The export/SEZ treatment is captured twice in two different vocabularies that can disagree, and the Compliance panel reads only the wrong one
findings.evidence: The invoice carries `supply_type` + `invoice_type` (migration 268; set in components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:745-775 and read by domain/gst/classifier.py). The e-invoice record independently carries `gst_treatment` with a SEPARATE vocabulary — `regular | export_with_payment | export_without_payment | sez_with_payment | sez_without_payment | deemed_export` (apps/web/lib/invoices/compliance.ts:26-33; stored by domain/income_tax/einvoice_service.py:76-83). CompliancePanel.tsx:51-53 builds its view from `gst_treatment: irn.record?.gst_treatment ?? null` and hardcodes `is_reverse_charge: null`, ignoring `invoice.is_reverse_charge`, which is present on the same `InvoiceDetail` object (apps/web/lib/invoices/gst.ts:115). Nothing reconciles the two vocabularies.
findings.ca_experience: The CA classifies an invoice as SEZ without payment in the editor. Opening the same invoice's Compliance panel, the GST treatment reads "Regular · B2B · Inter-state (IGST)" until they pick the treatment a second time while preparing the IRN — and even then the two records can permanently disagree, with GSTR-1 following one and the e-invoice record the other. Reverse charge never shows on the panel at all.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime holds one "Nature of transaction" per voucher that drives the return, the e-invoice JSON and the print alike; there is no second, independent classification.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive `gst_treatment` from the invoice's `supply_type` + `invoice_type` when preparing an IRN record (pre-fill and disable the picker), and pass `invoice.is_reverse_charge` into `compInv` instead of `null`. Longer term, drop `einvoice_records.gst_treatment` as an independent field.

findings.title: No GST compensation cess on a sales line
findings.evidence: `client_sales_invoice_lines` (migrations/050_sales_purchase_cycle.sql:58-74, plus every later ALTER — none adds one) has no cess column, and `InvoiceLineIn` (models/invoices.py:33-58) has no cess field. The GSTR-1 builder already expects one and says so: domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:634-636 — "Latent today — client_sales_invoice_lines has no cess column, so line cess is always 0 — but wrong the moment one is added." `_compute_line_gst` (routers/sales_invoices.py:167-193) returns only CGST/SGST/IGST.
findings.ca_experience: A client dealing in aerated drinks, tobacco, coal, or motor vehicles cannot raise a compliant invoice at all — the cess simply cannot be charged. Their GSTR-1 `csamt` is zero on every row and GSTR-3B under-declares the cess liability. The CA has to keep those clients on Tally.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all support compensation cess (ad valorem and per-unit) as a separate head on the line.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `cess_rate_bps` and `cess_paise` to the line and `cess_paise` to the header, include it in `_compute_line_gst`, in `journal_for_sales_invoice` (a Cess Output ledger), in the mirror `lib/money/gstLine.ts` and in the parity vectors. The GSTR-1 builder already reads `inv.cess_paise` / `line.cess_paise`.

findings.title: No quotation, proforma invoice, sales order or delivery challan — the sales cycle starts at the tax invoice
findings.evidence: `grep -rln "quotation|proforma|delivery_challan|sales_order|estimate" apps/api/routers apps/api/services apps/api/domain apps/api/models apps/api/migrations` returns only unrelated hits (task templates, payroll, income tax, workflow, inventory). The Sales page's tabs are Invoices, Recurring, Customers, Receipts, Credit Notes, Debit Notes, Statements (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:235-275). Nothing precedes the invoice.
findings.ca_experience: A trading or manufacturing client who sends goods on a delivery challan and invoices later, or who quotes before selling, cannot record either step. The CA either keeps a parallel book in Excel or keeps the client on Tally, which defeats the one-platform promise for exactly the SME segment being targeted.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime: Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Rejections In. Zoho Books: Estimates, Retainer Invoices, Sales Orders, Delivery Challans (with the GST delivery-challan format under Rule 55). Busy and Marg both have the full order-to-invoice chain.
findings.suggested_fix: Start with the delivery challan (Rule 55 — it is a statutory document with a prescribed format and it feeds e-way bills for movement without an invoice) and the quotation/estimate with a one-click convert-to-invoice. Sales orders can follow once inventory commitment is wanted.

findings.title: No HSN/SAC master is exposed — every firm builds its code library from zero before it can raise its first invoice
findings.evidence: routers/firm_hsn_library.py:1-13: "Caflow does not ship or expose a shared HSN/SAC master to users. Every code a firm bills against comes from THIS table". routers/hsn.py:3-11 confirms the search endpoint "used to merge in public.hsn_master ... It no longer does". migrations/175_hsn_master_official_expansion.sql:15-23 says the loaded backbone is 2-digit HSN chapters and 4-digit SAC groups plus some 6-digit SAC leaves — "The full 8-digit HSN leaf catalogue (~12k rows) is a large dataset best refreshed out-of-band". The dependency chain is enforced: every invoice line must reference a service_catalogue item (models/invoices.py:106-112, a hard 422), and the catalogue item's HSN comes from the firm library.
findings.ca_experience: On a new firm, the first invoice fails three times in a row — no catalogue item, then no HSN in the library, then the code has to be typed with its rate from memory or from the CBIC site. For a practice with 50 SME clients across trading, manufacturing and services, that is hundreds of codes entered by hand before any invoicing happens. It is the single biggest friction at first use and it lands before the product has proved anything.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all ship the full HSN/SAC master with GST rates and let you search it while typing a line; ClearTax has an HSN/rate finder. None asks the user to build the list.
findings.suggested_fix: Load the full CBIC HSN leaf catalogue and the SAC annexure into `hsn_master` (both are Government of India publications in the public domain, as migration 175 itself notes) and let the firm library's search offer them as "add from master" — keeping the firm's own curated list as the billing source, but seeding it in one click instead of one code at a time.

findings.title: No automated payment-reminder cadence to customers — the automatic run was removed and only a manual, one-invoice-at-a-time reminder remains
findings.evidence: services/collections_service.py:297-304 records the removal: "enabled/interval_days/max_reminders governed the automatic bulk cadence run (run_due_reminders), removed entirely: it looped every open invoice unbounded ... The manual, CA-initiated single-invoice send (send_invoice_reminder, below) is the only way a reminder goes out now". `send_overdue_reminders` (line 247) still runs in the nightly sweep but only writes a timeline entry (lines 276-283) — it sends the customer nothing. The manual path is `POST /api/sales-invoices/{id}/remind` (routers/sales_invoices.py:2093), driven one row at a time from the UI (app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:1655-1662). Delivery is email only (services/email_service.send_invoice_to_customer); nothing in the sales path touches WhatsApp.
findings.ca_experience: The owner's stated goal is to replace WhatsApp follow-ups. Today the CA still has to open each overdue invoice and click Remind, one by one, on a schedule they keep in their own head — which is the WhatsApp workflow with more clicks. There is no cadence (7/15/30 days), no escalation, no bulk send, and no channel the SME's customers actually read.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books has configurable automated payment reminders (before due, on due, and repeating after due) with per-customer opt-out; Zoho and Refrens both offer WhatsApp reminder delivery in India.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebuild the cadence bounded and resumable — a per-firm daily batch with a row cap and a cursor (the pattern `_paginate_all` and the bank "Pass N ready" chunking already use), keyed on `last_reminded_at` + `REMINDER_INTERVAL_DAYS`, sending the customer-facing reminder rather than a timeline entry. Add bulk Remind over the DataTable selection as an interim step (bulk Issue already exists at page.tsx:1607).

findings.title: Receipt and credit-note numbers take their financial year from today's date, not the document date
findings.evidence: services/receipt_service.py:56-61 `_current_fy()` reads `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and is used at line 549 (`fy = _current_fy()`) to build `receipt_no = f"RCPT-{fy}-{seq:04d}"` (line 621) — `data["receipt_date"]` is never consulted. routers/credit_notes.py:104-109 and :270 are identical for `CN-{fy}-…`, as is routers/sales_debit_notes.py:81-86 for `SDN-{fy}-…`. The FY-lock and period checks correctly use the document date (services/receipt_service.py:548), so only the NUMBER is wrong.
findings.ca_experience: Year-end data entry is when a CA touches the most receipts. Every March-dated receipt keyed in April is numbered `RCPT-2627-…` and sits in next year's series, out of order in the FY it belongs to. The same for credit notes. The CA discovers it when printing a year's receipt register and the numbers do not run.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime numbers a voucher from the voucher date's financial year, not the entry date; so do Zoho Books and Busy.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the FY label from the document's own date (`core.ist_clock` already has the helpers) in all three `_current_fy()` call sites. Note this changes numbering for back-dated documents going forward only — existing numbers stay as issued.

findings.title: No warning when a credit note is issued outside the §34(2) window, and no customer credit limit at all
findings.evidence: Two absences in the same area. (a) `issue_credit_note` (routers/credit_notes.py:464-660) checks the FY lock and the invoice's outstanding but never the §34(2) time limit; `compliance_engine.correction_window_closes()` exists and is the stated authority (CLAUDE.md; services/compliance_engine.py:196) but `grep -rn "correction_window" apps/api/routers` shows it is used only by the filing-demo flows, never by credit notes. (b) `customers` (migrations/049 → the CREATE TABLE at lines 4-27) has `credit_days` but no `credit_limit_paise`; migration 030 gave suppliers one (`030_supplier_tds_and_credit.sql:11,25`) and customers never got the equivalent. Nothing in `_create_invoice_core` checks a customer's exposure.
findings.ca_experience: (a) The CA issues a credit note in February 2027 against an FY 2025-26 invoice and the app accepts it silently. The receivable and the books reduce, but the GST liability cannot be reduced — the window closed on 30 November 2026 or on the date GSTR-9 was furnished, whichever was earlier — so the client pays tax on a supply that was credited. (b) A customer already ₹15,00,000 overdue can be invoiced again with nothing said.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and Zoho Books both warn when a credit note falls outside the amendment window. Tally Prime enforces a per-ledger Credit Limit and blocks or warns on a sales voucher that breaches it; Zoho Books shows a credit-limit warning on invoice creation.
findings.suggested_fix: (a) On credit-note issue, compare the note date with `correction_window_closes(fy_end_of_original_invoice)` and warn (not block — the commercial credit is still valid, only the tax adjustment is not), recording that the GST reduction is unavailable. (b) Add `customers.credit_limit_paise` and check it in `_create_invoice_core` against the customer's live outstanding, as a warning by default and a block when the firm turns that on.

findings.title: Nowhere in the sales screens can a CA see what a single invoice still owes
findings.evidence: The invoice list's columns are Invoice No, Date, Customer, Taxable, GST, Total, Due, Status (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/sales/page.tsx:1752-1778) — there is no balance/outstanding column, and the list query (line 1372) does not even select `credited_paise` or `debit_note_paise`. The receipt allocation screen shows the invoice TOTAL, not the outstanding: page.tsx:3606 `{inv.invoice_no} — {inv.invoice_date} — {fmtAmt(invoiceDisplayTotal(inv))}`, with the helper's own comment at :3418 admitting "(invoice total, not outstanding)". There is no auto-allocate-oldest-first control. Migration 278 added an `outstanding_paise` generated column precisely so this would be cheap, and no sales screen reads it.
findings.ca_experience: Collections is the daily job and the CA cannot do it from this screen. To answer "how much does this invoice still owe?" they open the invoice detail. To allocate a ₹2,00,000 receipt across four partly-paid invoices they must open each one first to find the balance, then type four numbers, with the screen showing them the full totals the whole time — which is how an over-allocation gets attempted and 422s.
findings.market_standard: Tally's Bills Outstanding shows pending amount per bill and auto-adjusts against the oldest; Zoho Books' invoice list has a Balance Due column and Record Payment pre-fills the balance per invoice with an "apply to oldest" option.
findings.suggested_fix: Select `outstanding_paise` (migration 278) and add a Balance column to the list, sortable. In the receipt allocator show the outstanding per invoice, pre-fill down to the receipt amount oldest-first with a one-click "Auto-allocate", and base the Unallocated line on amount + TDS − allocated.

findings.title: A line with no HSN/SAC silently prints 998211 — the CA-services SAC — on any invoice, including a goods invoice
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/invoice_pdf_service.py:29 `SAC_CODE = "998211"` ("professional/CA services", per the module docstring at line 11) and line 206 `line.get("hsn_sac") or SAC_CODE` — the fallback applies to every line of every sales invoice, not just the legacy fee-invoice path. `client_sales_invoice_lines.hsn_sac` is nullable (migrations/050_sales_purchase_cycle.sql:63) and `InvoiceLineIn.hsn_sac` is `Optional[str] = None` (models/invoices.py:35), so a blank is easy to produce; the editor treats HSN as an optional cell (components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:888-899) and `isValidLine` does not require it (lib/invoices/gst.ts:333-339).
findings.ca_experience: A trading client's invoice for steel pipes prints SAC 998211 — "Financial auditing services" — as the classification, because a line was saved without a code. The customer's GSTR-2B match fails on HSN, and the printed document misclassifies the supply under Rule 46(g). Nothing on screen ever showed the CA a code they did not enter.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime blocks the voucher ("HSN/SAC not specified") and lists it under Incomplete/Mismatch; Zoho Books warns before saving. None substitutes a default code.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the fallback in the sales path — print the cell blank so the omission is visible — and require `hsn_sac` on a line at issue time (a draft may still be incomplete). Keep `SAC_CODE` only for the legacy engagement-based fee invoice, which genuinely has no lines.

findings.title: E-invoice and e-way bill are record-keeping ledgers only — no JSON is produced, no applicability is determined, no validity or expiry is tracked
findings.evidence: domain/income_tax/einvoice_service.py:41-53 `ManualProvider.generate_irn` returns all-None; the module stores irn/ack_number/ack_date/qr_data typed in after the fact (lines 145-170). There is no e-invoice schema builder anywhere — `grep` finds no IRN JSON assembly. Nothing computes applicability: no AATO threshold check exists for e-invoicing, and the UI only advises "E-invoicing applies only above your firm's turnover threshold — confirm before generating" (apps/web/lib/invoices/compliance.ts:158). For e-way bills, `ewb_valid_upto` is typed in by the CA (routers/eway_bill.py:59 `ewb_valid_upto: str`) — Rule 138(10)'s one-day-per-200-km validity is never computed even though `distance_km` is captured (line 50), and nothing alerts before expiry. There is no /eway page at all; `grep -rn "eway" apps/web/app` finds only the audit-log label.
findings.ca_experience: The CA still generates every IRN and every e-way bill by re-keying the whole invoice into the IRP/NIC portal, then re-keys the result back here. The platform saves no data entry on the two highest-volume GST compliance actions, and it will not tell the CA which clients have crossed the e-invoicing threshold or which e-way bills expire tomorrow.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books generate the e-invoice JSON and the EWB JSON from the voucher for offline bulk upload even without a GSP, compute EWB validity from distance, and flag e-invoice applicability from the client's AATO. The bulk-generation tools on the government portals need no registration.
findings.suggested_fix: Two steps that need no GSP and break no rule in CLAUDE.md: (1) build the IRP e-invoice JSON and the EWB JSON from the invoice for download and manual upload, which is a pure prepare-only path exactly like the existing GSTR-1 JSON; (2) compute `ewb_valid_upto` from `distance_km` per Rule 138(10) and surface expiring bills on the deadlines view. Applicability from AATO is a separate, larger piece.

findings.title: An invoice can be created and issued with no place of supply, and only the GSTR-1 build discovers it months later
findings.evidence: routers/sales_invoices.py:672 `effective_supply_state = supply_state_code or customer.get("state_code") or ""` — an empty string is written to `client_sales_invoices.supply_state_code` (line 878) with no validation, and `issue_invoice` (line 1433) does not check it either. `SalesInvoiceIn.supply_state_code` is `Optional[str] = None` (models/invoices.py:136) with no state-code validator, and the editor's Supply State picker has no required marker (components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:713-716). It becomes an error only when the return is built: domain/gst/validator.py:93-99 rejects a place of supply not in `VALID_STATE_CODES`. The frontend has a `validatePlaceOfSupply` (lib/invoices/compliance.ts:97-118) but it runs only in the Compliance panel, never in the editor's `validateInvoiceEditor` (lib/invoices/gst.ts:341-364).
findings.ca_experience: Invoices go out all quarter with a blank place of supply — easy, since it is only auto-filled when the customer has a state code, and SALES-06 means several states cannot have one. On the 10th of the following month the CA builds GSTR-1 and gets a list of errors for invoices that are already issued, posted and sent to customers, each of which now needs a correction that cannot be a silent edit (CGST §34).
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime will not accept a GST sales voucher without Place of Supply; Zoho Books requires it on every invoice for a GST-registered organisation.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a valid 2-digit place of supply at issue time (not at draft), server-side in `issue_invoice` and mirrored in `validateInvoiceEditor` so the CA is stopped at the point of entry; default it from `customer.state_code` and, failing that, from `customer.gstin[:2]`.

findings.title: A credit note's is_interstate can be inherited from another client's invoice in the same firm
findings.evidence: routers/credit_notes.py:251-262: the lookup for the linked invoice filters on `.eq("id", data["sales_invoice_id"]).eq("firm_id", firm_id)` — client_id is not in the filter, unlike the equivalent read at issue time (line 528, which does filter `.eq("client_id", client_id)` and 422s). So at CREATE the note can silently take `is_interstate` from an invoice belonging to a different client of the same firm; the mismatch only surfaces when the CA tries to issue it.
findings.ca_experience: Rare, and it fails safe at issue. But the draft's computed CGST/SGST-vs-IGST split can be wrong from the moment it is created, so a CA reviewing the draft sees the wrong tax heads and a wrong total before the eventual refusal.
findings.market_standard: Not a market-comparison item — it is an internal scoping inconsistency against the same router's own later check.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `.eq("client_id", client_id)` to the create-path invoice lookup and 422 when it misses, matching the issue path.

findings.title: SalesInvoiceIn.place_of_supply is accepted by the API and silently ignored in production
findings.evidence: models/invoices.py:134 declares `place_of_supply: Optional[str] = None  # 2-digit state code`. In `_create_invoice_core` it is read ONLY on the mock branch (routers/sales_invoices.py:660-663, alongside a hardcoded `client_state_code = "27"`); the real branch at line 672 uses `supply_state_code or customer.state_code` and never looks at it. So the two branches decide intra- vs inter-state by different rules. The frontend and the CSV importer both send `supply_state_code` (InvoiceEditor.tsx:494; lib/invoices/importMapping.ts:237), so nothing in-product is broken today — but any integration reading the model would be.
findings.ca_experience: Not visible today. It matters to whoever writes the next integration or bulk-loader: they set the documented place of supply, the field is dropped, the customer master's state is used instead, and an invoice is taxed as intra-state that should be inter-state, with no error.
findings.market_standard: n/a — API hygiene.
findings.suggested_fix: Either fold `place_of_supply` into the real-branch resolution (`supply_state_code or place_of_supply or customer.state_code`) or delete the field from the model so it cannot be relied on. Aligning the mock branch's rule with the real one would also stop the two paths testing different logic.

findings.title: No TCS on sales, and the rate registry's note about §206C(1H) looks stale
findings.evidence: domain/tds/section_rates.py:142-149 carries a `"206C"` entry commented "TCS on sale of goods, Section 206C(1H) — unchanged, 0.1%" and immediately states "NOT wired to any computation anywhere in this codebase — confirmed zero readers ... do not assume TCS is an implemented feature because a rate exists here." Nothing in the sales path collects TCS: `_create_invoice_core` (routers/sales_invoices.py:640-960) has no TCS branch, `client_sales_invoices` has no TCS column, and `journal_for_sales_invoice` (services/phase2_journal_service.py:59-150) posts no TCS payable line. `_SECTIONS_2025_26` is used unchanged for FY 2026-27 (line 156).
findings.ca_experience: For a client dealing in scrap (§206C(1)), motor vehicles over ₹10 lakh (§206C(1F)) or overseas remittances (§206C(1G)), the invoice cannot collect TCS and there is no 27EQ data to file from. The CA keeps those clients elsewhere. Separately, a future implementer reading the "unchanged, 0.1%" note would build §206C(1H) collection for a provision I believe was omitted by the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 with effect from 1 April 2025 — I could not verify that against a primary source in this session, so treat the statutory point as needing confirmation, not the code reading.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Busy and Marg all support TCS on sales with the per-buyer threshold tracking and 27EQ data; Zoho Books supports TCS on invoices.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave TCS unbuilt until it is scoped (the comment is right that it is a feature, not a data gap). Do verify the §206C(1H) status against the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 and correct the comment either way — a wrong "unchanged" note in a rate registry is exactly the trap CLAUDE.md's annual-update section is written to prevent.

maturity.rationale: The transactional engine is genuinely strong and, in places, better than the market: every issue posts through the one kernel, money is integer paise end to end, receipt settlement is a single atomic RPC with CAS fallback, the frontend GST preview is pinned to the Python arithmetic by a generated fixture, tenant and client-assignment scoping is enforced on every route, and the GSTR-1 classification (supply type / invoice type / reverse charge / B2CL threshold by date) is more careful than most competitors. What is weak is everything the CA and their customer actually TOUCH. The tax invoice PDF — the deliverable, the legal document — names the CA practice as the supplier with the practice's own GSTIN, prints a hardcoded 18%/9%/9% rate regardless of the lines, states "reverse charge: No" unconditionally, omits quantity, unit, place of supply and the IRN/QR, and ignores every branding, template, bank-detail and footer setting the product lets a CA configure. Three market-standard essentials are simply absent: line discounts, automatic invoice numbering, and compensation cess. Several backend capabilities have no screen at all — receipt TDS, re-allocating an advance, GSTR-1 Table 11A. And one numbering defect (delete a middle draft credit note) permanently wedges a client's credit notes for the year. The gap is not depth of thinking — the code is unusually well-reasoned — it is that the last mile between a correct ledger entry and a correct document was never closed.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: Not yet — a CA would try to send the first invoice, see their own practice's GSTIN printed as the supplier on their client's sale with a hardcoded 18% tax rate and no logo, and stop there.

open_questions_for_owner: The invoice PDF builder was written for the practice's own fee invoices (`fee_invoices`) and reused for clients' sales invoices without re-pointing the supplier block. Was the sales-invoice PDF ever printed and looked at by a CA against a real client's invoice, or has it only ever been exercised through the API and the tests? The answer changes whether SALES-01/02/03 are one afternoon's fix plus a proof-read, or a sign that the whole print path needs an owner.

Sales invoice numbering was decided as 'fully manual, no generated scheme' and that decision is recorded in three places. Was it a deliberate product judgement about CAs owning their clients' series, or a deferral? The Settings → Invoice Settings screen (prefix / FY / sequence / starting number) exists, is reachable, and is read by nothing on this path — so today the product asks for a decision it then ignores. Which way do you want it resolved: build auto-numbering, or take the screen down?

Who is the invoicing user you are optimising for — the CA keying a client's back-book from vouchers, or the CA's SME client raising invoices themselves through the portal? The current editor (Product/Service mandatory on every line, HSN from a library the firm must build, invoice number typed by hand) is priced for the first and would defeat the second. Discounts, auto-numbering, branding and the delivery challan are all far more urgent for the second.

The firm HSN/SAC library starts empty by design, and `hsn_master` is populated but deliberately not exposed. What was the reasoning against shipping the CBIC master (a public-domain dataset) as a seedable source? If it was rate accuracy, note that the library's stored rate is already a pre-fill hint that never touches tax math — so seeding descriptions and codes alone would remove most of the onboarding friction without asserting a rate.

Automatic customer dunning was removed because the unbounded loop could starve the nightly sweep. Do you want it rebuilt bounded, and if so on what channel? Email-only reminders will not replace WhatsApp follow-ups, which is the stated goal — and a WhatsApp channel is a commercial integration (BSP, template approval), not a coding task, so it needs deciding before the cadence is designed around it.

Compensation cess, TCS, discounts, delivery challans and quotations each unlock a specific client type (FMCG/coal/auto, scrap dealers, traders, manufacturers). Which of those client types are actually in the target book? Migration 286 and the AA analysis suggest the live book is seven clients, all companies/LLPs/firms on current accounts — if the real segment is professional-services SMEs, discounts and auto-numbering matter far more than cess and TCS, and the ranking above should change.

Two independent classifications of the same export/SEZ fact now exist (`supply_type`+`invoice_type` on the invoice, `gst_treatment` on the e-invoice record). Which one do you want to be the single truth? Collapsing them is cheap now and expensive after either has real data behind it.

The e-invoice and e-way modules today only record what a human did on a portal. Building the IRP/EWB JSON for offline bulk upload needs no GSP, no registration and breaks none of the never-auto-submit rules — is that deliberately out of scope, or simply not reached yet?
strengths: One posting kernel, honoured without exception. Issue, cancel, credit note, sales debit note and receipt all route through `services/phase2_journal_service` — routers/sales_invoices.py:1489 posts the journal FIRST and only then flips the status, so a Chart-of-Accounts failure leaves a re-tryable draft rather than an issued-but-unposted invoice; cancellation reverses through the kernel (routers/sales_invoices.py:1622) and never rewrites the original.

Receipt settlement is genuinely atomic in production. `settle_receipt_atomic` (migration 160, called at services/receipt_service.py:497) posts the journal, the receipt row and every allocation's invoice update in one database transaction; the pre-atomic path is preserved for test doubles with a compare-and-set retry loop (lines 690-720) and a compensating reversal that refuses to reverse a journal another receipt already claims (lines 340-355). The reasoning behind each of those guards is written down beside it.

Frontend/backend money parity is real, not aspirational. `apps/web/lib/money/gstLine.ts` mirrors the Python arithmetic operation for operation — floor-then-split, BigInt exact-decimal truncation to match `Decimal(str(qty))` — and `shared/gst-parity-vectors.json` is GENERATED from the backend functions (apps/api/tests/generate_gst_parity_vectors.py) and asserted from both suites (apps/api/tests/test_gst_parity_vectors.py, apps/web/lib/money/gstLine.parity.test.ts). The preview a CA sees cannot disagree with what is saved.

The CGST+SGST split is computed correctly. `_compute_line_gst` (routers/sales_invoices.py:167-193) floors the FULL tax first and then halves it, so CGST+SGST always equals the IGST an identical inter-state supply would attract, with SGST carrying the odd paise — and the same fix was carried into credit_notes.py:139-149 rather than left to drift.

GSTR-1 classification is plumbed end to end and is more careful than most. Migration 268 gave the invoice supply_type / invoice_type / is_reverse_charge, the editor sets all three (components/invoices/InvoiceEditor.tsx:745-775), recurring templates stamp them onto every generated occurrence (services/recurring_invoice_service.py:485-489), and reverse charge reaches the return's `rchrg` flag (domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:232). The B2CL rule is date-aware — Notification 12/2024's ₹1 lakh from 01-08-2024, tested on INVOICE VALUE not taxable value (domain/gst/classifier.py:29-63).

Immutability after issue is enforced and explained. `_SOFT_UPDATE_FIELDS` (routers/sales_invoices.py:1556) limits a post-issue PATCH to reference/notes/due date/terms plus line units, the editor mirrors it so the CA never fills in a form that will be rejected (InvoiceEditor.tsx:126, 440-460), and cancellation is refused outright when receipts, credit notes or debit notes are attached (routers/sales_invoices.py:1596-1603).

Client-assignment scoping is enforced on every route, with the reasoning for it preserved. routers/sales_invoices.py:40-108 documents exactly what was reachable before and adds `_assert_invoice_scope` (404, never 403, so the status is not an id oracle) plus `_assert_batch_scope`, which checks every distinct client in a bulk payload before ANY row is written.

Reporting-performance discipline is followed here too. The invoice list batch-fetches lines in one query rather than N+1 (routers/sales_invoices.py:474-482); the customer statement asks the database for the opening position via `party_opening_position` (migration 282) and then bounds the document reads to the printed window (services/customer_statement_service.py:243-256), degrading to a full replay rather than to a wrong number.

The credit-note / debit-note sub-ledger is coherent and CAS-guarded. `credited_paise` and `debit_note_paise` are applied under compare-and-set with rollback of both the allocation row and the invoice on a journal failure (routers/credit_notes.py:521-585), and the settlement ceiling `(total + debit notes) − paid − credited` is used identically in the receipt path, the re-allocation path and the statement — one formula, three call sites, no drift.

The multi-currency sales path is thought through. The document currency is frozen at creation and reconstructed from the stored row on edit rather than re-resolved (routers/sales_invoices.py:1278-1280), the base total is defined as the SUM of the converted components so the GL balances with no FX-rounding plug (lines 754-762), and a foreign receipt relieves each invoice at ITS booked rate with the difference posted to realized FX in one balanced journal (services/receipt_service.py:145-175).

Recurring invoicing is correctly conservative: draft only, never auto-issued, never auto-emailed, generated through the SAME `create_invoice` endpoint so GST, FY-lock and validation are identical to a manual invoice (services/recurring_invoice_service.py:1-21, 499-505), with a unique (template, occurrence) constraint and a self-cleaning duplicate path (lines 400-416).

The GST advance service refuses rather than guessing, and says so in its payload. `advances_report` returns `table_11_computed: false` with a plain-English `why` (services/gst_advance_service.py:228-243) explaining Notification 66/2017 and the goods/services split — a CA reading an empty Table 11 learns whether it is empty because there were no advances or because nothing computes it. (The refusal is right; that the computing path is unreachable is SALES-09.)
subsystem: Sales cycle: customers, sales invoices, credit/debit notes, receipts and allocation, recurring invoices, customer statements, party credits, invoice PDF/templates/branding, e-invoice and e-way bill records, service catalogue and HSN library
test_coverage_notes:
Volume is high and the quality of individual tests is good, but the coverage has a consistent shape: the ledger is tested hard, the document is not, and several tests pin behaviour that no user action can reach.

What is well covered. `tests/test_e2e_sales_cycle.py` drives the real endpoints against a FakeDB through create → issue → receipt and asserts the trial balance ties, AR nets to zero, and Bank is debited — and it exercises the REAL (non-mock) branch, so `test_sales_cycle_interstate_uses_igst` (line 124) genuinely covers the client-GSTIN-vs-customer-state derivation of `is_interstate`. `tests/test_invoice_round_off.py` proves CGST+SGST equals the IGST equivalent for odd tax, that the round-off delta stays in [-49,+50], and that the journal balances in all four rounding cases. `shared/gst-parity-vectors.json` is generated from the backend and asserted from both suites. Client-scope isolation has a dedicated file per router (test_invoice_bill_client_scope, test_receipts_client_scope, test_oos2_sales_invoice_scope, test_customers_client_scope, test_recurring_client_scope, test_eway_bill_client_scope). Concurrency and atomicity have their own real-Postgres files (test_r2_12_atomic_receipt_settlement_pg, test_r227_settle_receipt_atomic_status_guard_pg, test_r2_9_document_numbering_pg). I ran tests/test_phase2_sales_cycle.py, test_credit_notes.py, test_sales_debit_notes.py, test_invoice_round_off.py and test_gstr1_classification_from_invoice.py: 115 passed in 0.99s.

Tests that pin the wrong thing. `tests/test_invoice_pdf_line_items.py:193` stubs `_load_firm` to return `{"name": "Test & Co", "gstin": "27AAAAA9999A1Z5"}` and then asserts the rendered PDF is correct — it locks in SALES-01, the CA firm appearing as the supplier on a client's sale. Nothing in test_invoice_pdf.py or test_invoice_pdf_line_items.py asserts the printed TAX RATE, so the hardcoded 18%/9%/9% (SALES-02) and the unconditional "reverse charge: No" (SALES-03) are invisible to CI.

Tests that cover unreachable code. `tests/test_gstr1_advances_are_surfaced.py:163` seeds `gst_rate_bps` and `place_of_supply` directly into the receipts table to exercise Table 11A/11B — a state no API call or screen can produce (SALES-09). The feature is green and dead.

Gaps. Nothing tests numbering after a delete: `tests/test_document_numbering_unit.py` covers only that `_next_cn_seq` is per-client, and no test creates three notes, deletes the middle draft and creates a fourth — the exact sequence that wedges numbering permanently (SALES-04, which I reproduced against that file's own FakeDB). No test asserts what the Sales page's Outstanding tile computes (SALES-05). No test covers a supply_type / reverse-charge classification against a non-zero tax rate (SALES-16), an empty place of supply reaching issue (SALES-29), or `period_lock_service` on the credit-note / debit-note / receipt paths (SALES-15). The frontend statutory module `lib/invoices/compliance.ts` has a test (compliance.test.ts) but it ASSERTS the taxable-value threshold at line 54-55, so it pins SALES-17 rather than catching it. `lib/invoices/gst.ts`'s duplicate INDIAN_STATES list has no test at all, which is why six live state codes can go missing (SALES-06).
what_exists:
Backend. `routers/sales_invoices.py` (2,144 lines) is the centre: create (single and `/bulk` for CSV import), draft PATCH with full GST recompute, `/issue` (posts through `phase2_journal_service.journal_for_sales_invoice` FIRST, then flips status), `/cancel` (Partner-only; refuses when receipts/credit/debit notes are attached; reverses through the kernel), draft-only DELETE, `/pdf`, `/send`, `/resend`, `/deliveries`, `/remind`, `/reminders`, `/hsn-suggestions`, `/outstanding`, and a `maintenance/unposted` + `/repost-journal` remediation pair. GST is computed per line in integer paise (`_compute_line_gst`: floor the full tax, then split, SGST carrying the odd paise), intra/inter decided by the CLIENT's GSTIN prefix vs the effective supply state. Invoice-level round-off to ₹1 is opt-in (migration 247) and posts to a Round Off ledger. Multi-currency freezes the rate at creation.
